_about: What the count of seas between two bases must be, and which passed strongholds must lie inside bombers' reach of a field held behind them: the Pacific planner's test on paper (ruling 173, riders (b) and (m); ruling 181), kept with the map so that every build is judged by it (tools/check-reach.mjs). within and beyond are [from, to, seas, why], counted as the rules count: a fleet reaches the seas of its base and two beyond, a landing crosses three seas at most, the first and the last counted. names gives the chart's name for a place the planner calls otherwise. standin gives the sea or seas a place is taken to stand on until its province is drawn. passed is [stronghold, fields held behind it]: one of them must lie within reach km of it, measured from province centre to province centre along the map's line, the planner's own measure (on the far side the rules read the globe's distance: '_ranges' says what that moves). flights is [from, to, km as the planner measured it between its own points, fighters or bombers, the reaches tried] (ruling 184): on the chart each flight must fall as it fell on paper at every reach, in full, in part or out of reach for fighters (air.ts, cover: in full to six tenths of the reach), within or beyond for bombers. coasts is the sea or seas each island and each coast of the two roads must stand on, and no others: one sea for a small island, so that one fight decides whether it is fed, two for Rabaul, Bougainville, New Georgia and the Lae coast, which were ringed from both sides (ruling 181, point 4).
within: Japan's carriers reach Pearl Harbor from the Kuriles, as they sailed
the Midway landing force sailed from Saipan
and the fleet from home waters
America's carrier raid of April 1942 needs Midway held
the fleet at Truk can strike a landing in the Marshalls
why Japan built the field: Fiji, Samoa and New Caledonia come into reach from it
the Marianas from the Marshalls' anchorage
Japan's plan was for the fleet at Truk to answer a landing in the Gilberts or the Marshalls
the carriers that struck Rabaul on 11 November 1943 sailed from Espiritu Santo
the carriers that struck Palau in March 1944 sailed from the Marshalls' anchorage
and those that covered Hollandia in April 1944
the Palau landing force sailed from the Guadalcanal anchorages
the cruisers at Brisbane covered Port Moresby in the Coral Sea
but an enemy fleet based on Oahu reaches California: Hawaii is the shield
beyond: a fleet from Pearl Harbor cannot enter Japan's home waters: Midway is the step (its carriers can still raid from the sea next door, as in April 1942)
nor a fleet from Tokyo Bay Hawaii's: the Kuriles or the Marshalls are the step
the West Coast needs Hawaii to reach further
and no enemy fleet reaches California while Hawaii stands
the Marianas need a forward anchorage
the Solomons need the South Pacific bases
the Marianas are not a hop from the Gilberts
Leyte needs Hollandia, Palau or Ulithi
Hawaii is out of Truk's reach
California is out of reach of a fleet in the Marshalls
_ranges: The ranges as laid by the record (the design director's rulings of 11:26Z and 11:46Z of 22 November 2026, on the historian's far-reach-radii.md; laid in far-air.json by tools/make-far-air.mjs, the far side's switch only). A type's reach is the farthest radius the record flew as routine, more than once and at its ordinary load. The figure laid is the flight that sets it, measured as the rules measure, from province centre to province centre on the globe, because a staff weighs in the game's own measure; the record's own figure, from the field to the target, stands beside it here. Japan's fighters (from September 1940, the A6M2's first month) and its bombers: 1,048 km, Rabaul to Guadalcanal, the A6M2 with its drop tank and the G4M1, August to November 1942; the record's 1,044. America's bombers, and 'reach' below for the passed strongholds, which stands for the same aircraft: 1,243 km, Eniwetok to Truk, the B-24, September and October 1944; the record's 1,228. America's escorts: 1,250 km from October 1944, inside the record's routine of 1,221 to 1,323 (Morotai to Balikpapan by order from 3 October 1944, Saipan to Truk, Iwo Jima to Tokyo); before it an escort reaches as cover does, 550, which stands until its rows are sourced. The long bombers' 2,550 stands: the record's Chengtu to Yawata is 2,533 and Saipan to Tokyo 2,362. Britain's, Australia's, the Dutch and China's groups fly air.json's figures until sourced rows come. Readings, flown and not the reach: Kendari to Darwin, 1,313 km in the record and 1,350 on the chart, flown once on 19 February 1942 and out of routine reach; Balikpapan from Noemfoor and Darwin, 2,000 to 2,100 km, a few raids with cut loads; Morotai to Balikpapan, 1,323 in the record and 1,355 on the chart, beyond the escorts' 1,250; the A6M3 Model 32's shorter months from August 1942; the G4M1's armour of March 1943, which follows when the historian gives it as a radius. By type, where a row carries one (the design director, 12:50Z of 22 November 2026, on the historian's section 7): Japan's navy land bombers, the G3M and the G4M, on the air flotillas' and air fleets' rows, 1,181 km, Kwajalein to Wake (1,180.03 on the chart; the record's 1,103 from Roi-Namur, at least seven raids in fourteen days of December 1941), with Saigon to Singapore, 1,102 on the chart and five raids in seven weeks, inside it; the army's bombers stand at 1,048 until sourced. The Dutch B-25s under Australian command (No. 18 Squadron NEI): 806 km, Darwin to Koepang (the record's 863 from Batchelor to Penfui, over 900 sorties from May 1943). The Beaufighter's Coomalie Creek to Penfoei, 871 and routine, has no row of its own to stand on. Truk to Rabaul, 1,298 on the chart, is not shown as a land bombers' raid and does not count. On the globe one passed stronghold lies beyond 1,243 of every field behind it: Marcus Island (Iwo Jima 1,281, Saipan 1,328, Wake 1,421). The flights below keep the planner's own measure on its paper and the reaches it tried (ruling 184), and tools/check-reach.mjs judges the chart against the paper by the map's line as before: it is not the game's reach.
